subject: LumenBank post-demo: recommended model shortlist, tradeoffs, and operational risks
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@lumenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: LumenBank post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Hi Anya — thanks again for taking the demo today. Appreciate the clear framing on: fraud-flagging latency targets (p95 < 120ms), and the requirement to keep false positives < 3% on the retail card flow. Quick recap and recommended next steps below.

Key takeaways from the call:
- Target profile: low-latency, high-throughput inference for short sequences (avg 40 tokens).
- Data residency: US-only, log-level audit required for compliance team.
- Budget sensitivity: procurement prefers a model profile that keeps unit cost predictable under sustained QPS.

Post-demo recommended shortlist (tradeoffs summarized):
1) LlamaX-13B-int8
   - Pros: Best cost/throughput for batch inference; reasonable quality after prompt tuning; available in our Dedicated pool.
   - Cons: Slightly higher hallucination risk on rare policy language; requires prompt-set calibration.
   - Typical latency (p95): ~90–110ms (with Redwood batching + KV cache).
2) Falcon-40B-4bit-qat (reduced)
   - Pros: Highest plausibility/precision on few-shot classification; fewer false positives in our evals.
   - Cons: Higher unit cost and memory footprint; p95 latency closer to 140–180ms unless colocated on high-spec GPUs.
3) OpenAssistant-7B-quant
   - Pros: Lowest cost; great for fallback scoring and syntactic cleanup; best for embedding/rerank cheap pass.
   - Cons: Quality gaps on edge cases; not recommended as single-model production path.

Attached: preliminary benchmark sweep (lumenbank_benchmarks_q2.csv) and the prompt pack we used (prompt_set_v1.txt). The benchmark sheet has per-model p50/p95 token latencies, cost-per-1M-tokens estimate under Redwood pricing, and a short QA column with observed FP rates on the seed dataset you shared.

Open/regression risks to call out:
- Quality regression: When we quantize LlamaX aggressively (int8) some behavioral shifts on long-tail policy language appear — suggested mitigation: static prompt anchors + a small regression test set (10–20 examples) you sign off on.
- Operational: Falcon-40B will need a dedicated node configuration to hit the latency SLO; recommended capacity: 2x 80GB A100 nodes for steady QPS 350–500.

Proposed next steps:
- You: confirm a ~10–12 example regression set we can use for QA (deadline: Tue 8/18).
- Us: run a 48-hour dedicated benchmark for Falcon-40B if you want a hard latency SLA estimate (cost estimate included in the attached MA draft).
- Procurement: if you want pricing for Dedicated vs Hosted for Falcon, I can loop in our sales ops.

If agreeable, I’ll share a short MA (mutual action) doc with milestones and a recommended pilot configuration (2 models: LlamaX for primary, OpenAssistant as fallback).

Thanks — Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: lumenbank_benchmarks_q2.csv (text/csv)]
[Attachment: prompt_set_v1.txt (text/plain)]

From: Anya Petrov <anya@lumenbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LumenBank post-demo recap + recommended model shortlist

Thanks Sofia — this is super helpful. A few quick clarifying Qs before we carve out the regression set: 

1) For the LlamaX-13B-int8 path, can you confirm whether the hallucination cases you saw are recoverable with prompt anchors alone, or do we need to do a small fine-tune / RLHF pass?
2) For Falcon-40B, you mentioned a 2x 80GB node baseline — is that assuming 1:1 redundancy or active-active? We’d like to size for peak QPS during month-end.
3) Procurement will want an itemized delta between Hosted vs Dedicated for the Falcon baseline — can you provide a simple delta table (price / SLA / data separation)?

I’ll pull together a 12-example regression set we can share by Monday EOD. Also looping in procurement (procurement@lumenbank.com) for the pricing ask.

—Anya
Anya Petrov
Head of Fraud Analytics | LumenBank

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: LumenBank follow-ups (shortlist + asks)

Looping in the ops/solutions thread. Quick notes for our responses to Anya: 

- LlamaX hallucination: likely recoverable with prompt anchors + guardrail rerank. Fine-tune probably unnecessary for initial pilot; recommend: 2-week prompt-tuning sprint and a regression harness (12 examples Anya will provide). If we still see >2% FP, then escalate to a small (few-hour) fine-tune evaluation with sanitized examples (TTR).

- Falcon sizing: recommendation is active-active for month-end headroom. 2x 80GB assumes active-active with autoscale headroom. Put a note in the MA draft for a burst + pre-warm policy to avoid cold-starts.

- Pricing delta table: Karthik, can you draft a short Hosted vs Dedicated delta (3 lines: unit cost @ sustained 1M tokens/day, SLA p95/uptime, data separation) that Sofia can send to procurement?

- Attach to MA draft: a simple runbook for regression detection (how we’ll run daily evals, alerting thresholds, rollback policy). See below bullet skeleton for the runbook to paste into the MA.

Runbook skeleton (paste-ready):
- Daily small-batch regression job against the 12-example guardrail set (p95 latency, FP rate).
- Alert: FP rate > 2% for 24h or FP delta > +0.8% vs baseline -> trigger canary rollback to OpenAssistant fallback.
- Escalation: CS lead + engineering on call; Redwood will hold a triage in 30–60 minutes.

I’ll prep the MA draft and a short benchmark explainer for Anya.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: ma_plan_draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@lumenbank.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: LumenBank post-demo: recommended model shortlist, tradeoffs, and operational risks

Hi Anya — thanks for the quick reply and for pulling procurement in. Short answers to your Qs below and attached the delta table link: https://redwood-inference.internal/benchmarks/LB-0814 (public within our GDrive).

1) LlamaX hallucinations: from our initial runs, prompt anchors + 1‑pass rerank reduced hallucinations by ~70%. For your risk tolerance (FP < 3%), prompt tuning + the daily regression harness should be sufficient to start. We can plan a 2-week validation phase before considering any fine-tune.

2) Falcon sizing: recommendation is active-active. The 2x80GB baseline provides sustained headroom for monthly spikes ~500 QPS with p95 ~140ms. If you need p95 < 120ms with Falcon we should discuss colocating on 2x H100s (higher cost).

3) Hosted vs Dedicated delta (high level):
- Hosted: lower startup friction, pay-as-you-go, no infra management; SLA: shared 99.9% with latency best-effort; Data separation: logical separation (suitable if you can accept provider-managed isolation).
- Dedicated: higher commit, predictable throughput and better p95 guarantees, SLA: 99.95% with pinned capacity, Data separation: tenant-dedicated pools and VPC options.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Mon 8/17: Lumen provides 12 regression examples.
- Tue 8/18–Wed 8/19: Redwood runs prompt-tuning + 48-hr benchmark on LlamaX-13B-int8. Share results and FP metrics.
- Thu 8/20: Decision checkpoint — if FP < 3% and latency within targets, proceed with 2-week pilot (LlamaX primary + OpenAssistant fallback). Otherwise, schedule Falcon dedicated benchmark.

We’ll attach the MA doc and the Hosted vs Dedicated delta table in the next email. If procurement wants a formal quote, I can route a procurement-ready estimate.

Thanks again — looking forward to the sample set.

Best,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Signed-off: Marissa Cole, Director, Solutions Engineering]
